title: ESTILO INDIRECTO
subtitle: Reported statements · contar lo que alguien dijo

map.center: Usamos el ESTILO INDIRECTO para contar lo que otra persona dijo, sin comillas y con cambios.

nodes.title: ¿Siempre cambia?
items: Si sigue siendo verdad, no hace falta: He said he lives in Rome.
Con says (presente), no cambia: She says she's tired.

error.title: Error común
bad: She said me that she was tired.
good: She told me that she was tired.

mini.es: Pasa a estilo indirecto (un paso atrás).

items.q: “I'm tired.” → She said she ___ tired.
“I'll call you.” → He said he ___ call me.
“We can't come.” → They said they ___ come.
She ___ me she was leaving. (say / tell)
“I saw it.” → He said he ___ it.

explain.es: El estilo indirecto (reported speech) sirve para contar lo que otra persona dijo sin repetir sus palabras exactas ni usar comillas. Como lo contamos después, desde otro momento y a veces desde otro lugar, casi siempre hay que ajustar tres cosas: el tiempo verbal, los pronombres y las expresiones de tiempo y lugar. En español pasa lo mismo: «Estoy cansada» → Dijo que estaba cansada. (Las preguntas y las órdenes indirectas tienen su propio mapa.)
explain.en: Reported speech tells what someone said without quoting their exact words. We usually change the tense, the pronouns and the time and place words.

explain.title: 1 · SAY y TELL
explain.es: Los dos verbos significan decir, pero se construyen distinto. Tell necesita a quién se lo dices justo detrás y sin to: tell me, tell her, tell the class. Say no lleva persona; si la quieres añadir, usa to: say something to someone. La palabra that es opcional y en la conversación se suele omitir.
explain.en: tell + person (no to): She told me… say + no person, or say to + person. That is optional.

examples.en: He said nothing to his parents about the accident.
examples.es: No les dijo nada a sus padres sobre el accidente.

explain.title: Truco: la máquina del tiempo
explain.es: Imagina que said es una máquina del tiempo que empuja todo un paso hacia el pasado: is → was, will → would, did → had done. Y para say / tell: Tell lleva Tu persona (tell me, tell him); say va solo.
explain.en: said pushes everything one step into the past. Tell takes a person; say stands alone.

explain.title: 2 · Un paso atrás
explain.es: Cuando el verbo que introduce (said, told) está en pasado, el verbo de lo que se dijo retrocede un tiempo: el presente pasa a pasado; el pasado y el present perfect pasan a past perfect; will pasa a would. Es lógico: lo que era «ahora» para quien habló ya es «antes» para quien lo cuenta. Es la misma concordancia de tiempos del español (dijo que trabajaba).
explain.en: After a past reporting verb, the tense usually <mark>moves one step back</mark>: present → past, past / present perfect → past perfect, will → would.

examples.en: “I work in a bank.” → He said he worked in a bank.
examples.es: «Trabajo en un banco». → Dijo que trabajaba en un banco.

examples.en: “We're moving to Leeds.” → They said they were moving to Leeds.
examples.es: «Nos mudamos a Leeds». → Dijeron que se mudaban a Leeds.

examples.en: “I lost my keys.” → She said she had lost her keys.
examples.es: «Perdí las llaves». → Dijo que había perdido las llaves.

explain.title: 3 · Los modales
explain.es: will → would, can → could, may → might. Must de obligación suele pasar a had to (también puede quedarse como must). Would, could, should, might y ought to se quedan igual.
explain.en: will → would, can → could, may → might, must → had to (or must). would, could, should, might and ought to don't change.

examples.en: “I'll send it tomorrow.” → She said she would send it the next day.
examples.es: «Lo enviaré mañana». → Dijo que lo enviaría al día siguiente.

examples.en: “You must wear a helmet.” → The instructor said we had to wear a helmet.
examples.es: «Tenéis que llevar casco». → El monitor dijo que teníamos que llevar casco.

examples.en: “You should see a doctor.” → My mum said I should see a doctor.
examples.es: «Deberías ir al médico». → Mi madre dijo que debería ir al médico.

head: Directo · Direct
Indirecto · Reported
Ejemplo directo
Ejemplo indirecto
rows: He said he was going to quit.
explain.note: would, could, should, might, ought to y el past perfect no cambian: ya no pueden ir más atrás. El cambio past simple → past perfect es opcional si el orden de los hechos está claro: He said he met her in 2019 también es correcto.
explain.note_en: would, could, should, might, ought to and the past perfect never change.

explain.title: 4 · Pronombres y posesivos
explain.es: Los pronombres cambian según quién lo cuenta y a quién, exactamente como en español: si Ana dice «Me encanta mi trabajo», tú cuentas «Dijo que le encantaba su trabajo». Revisa siempre I, me, my, we, our, you, your: suelen pasar a he / she, him / her, his / her, they, their… o a I, me, my si te lo dijeron a ti.
explain.en: Pronouns and possessives change according to who is reporting: I → he / she, my → his / her, you → I / me.

examples.en: “I love my job.” → Ana said she loved her job.
examples.es: «Me encanta mi trabajo». → Ana dijo que le encantaba su trabajo.

examples.en: “We've sold our flat.” → They told me they had sold their flat.
examples.es: «Hemos vendido nuestro piso». → Me dijeron que habían vendido su piso.

examples.en: “You can borrow my car.” → Tom told me I could borrow his car.
examples.es: «Puedes coger mi coche». → Tom me dijo que podía coger su coche.

explain.title: 5 · Tiempo y lugar
head: Directo · Direct
Indirecto · Reported
rows: the next day / the following day
the day before / the previous day
the following week / the week after
the month before / the previous month
explain.note: Solo cambian si el momento o el lugar ya no son los mismos. Si lo cuentas el mismo día y en el mismo sitio, puedes dejar today o here.
explain.note_en: Change them only if the time or place is different when you report.

explain.title: SAY o TELL
explain.es: Además de para el estilo indirecto, say y tell forman expresiones fijas que conviene aprender de memoria: tell va con historias, mentiras, verdades e instrucciones; say va con palabras y fórmulas sociales.
explain.en: Learn the fixed expressions with say and tell.

cols.head: 🗨️ TELL
items: tell the truth / a lie / a story / a joke

explain.title: 6 · ¿Cuándo NO hay que cambiar?
explain.es:
No hace falta dar el paso atrás cuando:
• el verbo introductor está en presente (says, has said), por ejemplo al leer un mensaje o una noticia;
• lo dicho sigue siendo verdad ahora (es opcional);
• el verbo ya es past perfect o un modal como would, could, should, might.
explain.en: No backshift when the reporting verb is in the present (says), when the statement is still true (optional), or with past perfect, would, could, should, might.

examples.en: “I'm on the train.” → Ana says she's on the train.
examples.es: «Estoy en el tren». → Ana dice que está en el tren.

examples.en: “The Earth goes round the Sun.” → The teacher said the Earth goes round the Sun.
examples.es: El profesor dijo que la Tierra gira alrededor del Sol.

examples.en: “I live in Rome.” → He told me he lives / lived in Rome.
examples.es: Me dijo que vive / vivía en Roma. (sigue viviendo allí)

items.en: “I'm really nervous about the interview.” → Laura said she was really nervous about the interview.
items.es: Laura dijo que estaba muy nerviosa por la entrevista.

items.en: “We've never been to Scotland.” → They told us they had never been to Scotland.
items.es: Nos dijeron que nunca habían estado en Escocia.

items.en: “The 9.15 train will be delayed.” → A woman said the 9.15 train would be delayed.
items.es: Una mujer dijo que el tren de las 9.15 llegaría con retraso.

items.en: “I can't find my passport.” → My dad said he couldn't find his passport.
items.es: Mi padre dijo que no encontraba su pasaporte.

items.en: “I bought this jacket yesterday.” → She said she had bought that jacket the day before.
items.es: Dijo que se había comprado esa chaqueta el día anterior.

items.en: “I'm going to apply for the job.” → Mark told me he was going to apply for the job.
items.es: Mark me dijo que iba a presentarse al puesto.

items.en: “We may be late tonight.” → They said they might be late that night.
items.es: Dijeron que quizá llegarían tarde esa noche.

items.en: “You're doing a great job.” → My manager told me I was doing a great job.
items.es: Mi jefa me dijo que estaba haciendo un gran trabajo.

items.en: “I was watching the match when it happened.” → He said he had been watching the match when it happened.
items.es: Dijo que estaba viendo el partido cuando pasó.

items.en: “I don't like spicy food.” → My cousin said she didn't like spicy food.
items.es: Mi prima dijo que no le gustaba la comida picante.

items.en: “We'll have the meeting here tomorrow.” → He said they would have the meeting there the following day.
items.es: Dijo que tendrían la reunión allí al día siguiente.

items.en: “It's the best film I've ever seen.” → She told everyone it was the best film she had ever seen.
items.es: Les dijo a todos que era la mejor película que había visto nunca.

items.bad: She said me that she was tired.
items.why: say no lleva persona detrás; tell sí. (Calco de «me dijo».)

items.bad: He told that he was hungry.
items.good: He told me / He said (that) he was hungry.
items.why: tell siempre necesita a quién: tell me, tell us…

items.bad: My sister told to me that she was pregnant.
items.good: My sister told me (that) she was pregnant.

items.bad: Last month Ana said she will call me, but she never did.
items.good: Last month Ana said she would call me, but she never did.
items.why: Verbo introductor en pasado → will pasa a would.
items.why_en: will → would after a past reporting verb.

items.bad: They said they have finished the project.
items.good: They said they had finished the project.

items.bad: He said he had seen her yesterday. <small>(contado una semana después)</small>
items.good: He said he had seen her the day before.
items.why: Si lo cuentas otro día, yesterday → the day before.
Expresión fija: tell the truth / a lie / a story / a joke.
En estilo indirecto no hay comillas ni dos puntos.
items.why_en: No quotation marks in reported speech.

items.es: Mira el verbo introductor: ¿said / told (pasado)? Da el paso atrás. ¿says (presente)? No cambies el tiempo.
items.en: Past reporting verb → backshift; present → no change.

items.es: Elige say o tell: ¿dices a quién? → told me / told him. ¿No? → said.
Cambia el tiempo verbal un paso atrás: am → was, will → would, did → had done.
items.en: Move the tense one step back.

items.es: Cambia pronombres y posesivos según quién habla: I → she, my → her.
Cambia tiempo y lugar si hace falta: tomorrow → the next day, here → there.
items.en: Change time and place words if needed.

items.es: Quita las comillas y, si quieres, añade that.
items.en: Remove the quotation marks; that is optional.

lines.en: Guess what! I've just spoken to Mike from Marketing.
lines.es: ¡Adivina! Acabo de hablar con Mike, de Marketing.

lines.en: Oh yes? What did he say?
He told me he was leaving the company.
lines.es: Me ha dicho que se va de la empresa.

lines.en: Really? Last month he said he loved his job!
lines.es: ¿En serio? ¡El mes pasado dijo que le encantaba su trabajo!

lines.en: I know. But he said he had received a better offer from a company in Dublin.
lines.es: Ya. Pero me ha dicho que ha recibido una oferta mejor de una empresa de Dublín.

lines.en: Wow. When is he going to tell the boss?
lines.es: Vaya. ¿Y cuándo se lo va a decir al jefe?

lines.en: He said he was going to tell her tomorrow. Oh no… he said it was a secret!
lines.es: Ha dicho que se lo iba a decir mañana. Ay, no… ¡dijo que era un secreto!

lines.en: Don't worry. I didn't hear a thing!

explain.note: Hazlo siempre en este orden y revisa al final: ¿say o tell? ¿He quitado las comillas?

items.q: “I'm tired.” → She said me she was tired.
items.why: say + no person → She told me / She said (that)…

items.q: “Water boils at 100°C.” → The teacher said water boils at 100°C.
items.why: It's still true, so no change is needed.

items.q: “I'll help you tomorrow.” <small>(contado un mes después)</small> → He said he would help me the next day.
“I'm on the bus.” → Ana says she's on the bus.
“I had already eaten.” → He said he had already eaten.
“We're leaving now.” <small>(contado al día siguiente)</small> → They said they were leaving now.
“I can't swim.” → She told that she couldn't swim.
items.why: tell needs a person: She told me… / She said…

items.q: “I bought it here.” <small>(contado en otra ciudad)</small> → He said he had bought it there.

exercises.title: Ordena la frase
exercises.es: Ordena las palabras para formar frases en estilo indirecto.

items.q: told / she / me / was / she / tired
items.a: She told me she was tired.

items.q: he / that / said / would / he / be / late
items.a: He said that he would be late.

items.q: they / us / told / had / they / moved / house
items.a: They told us they had moved house.

items.q: said / she / couldn't / she / the / find / keys
items.a: She said she couldn't find the keys.

items.q: my / boss / that / said / was / the / meeting / cancelled
items.a: My boss said that the meeting was cancelled.

items.q: told / she / day / me / the / had / before / she / arrived
items.a: She told me she had arrived the day before.

items.q: said / going / they / were / to / they / buy / a / flat
items.a: They said they were going to buy a flat.

items.q: a / joke / told / us / the / funny / teacher
items.a: The teacher told us a funny joke.

exercises.title: Pásalo a estilo indirecto
exercises.es: Lo cuentas varios días después. Empieza con las palabras dadas y cambia tiempos, pronombres y expresiones de tiempo.
exercises.en: Report the sentences a few days later.

items.q: “I'm studying for my exams,” said Lucía. → Lucía said…
items.a: Lucía said (that) she was studying for her exams.

items.q: “We've bought a new car,” my neighbours told me. → My neighbours told me…
items.a: My neighbours told me (that) they had bought a new car.

items.q: “I'll send you the report tomorrow,” said my colleague Ian. → Ian said…
items.a: Ian said (that) he would send me the report the next (following) day.

items.q: “I can't come to the meeting,” said Peter. → Peter said…
items.a: Peter said (that) he couldn't come to the meeting.

items.q: “I didn't take your phone,” my brother told me. → My brother told me…
items.a: My brother told me (that) he hadn't taken my phone.

items.q: “We're going to get married next year,” they told us. → They told us…
items.a: They told us (that) they were going to get married the following (next) year.

items.q: “I don't eat meat,” said Emma. → Emma said…
items.a: Emma said (that) she didn't eat meat. (También: doesn't eat, si sigue siendo verdad.)

items.q: “You must be at the airport two hours early,” the agent told us. → The agent told us…
items.a: The agent told us (that) we had to (must) be at the airport two hours early.

items.q: “I was sleeping when you called,” said Dad. → Dad said…
items.a: Dad said (that) he had been sleeping when I called (had called).

items.q: “This is the best pizza I've ever had,” said Nico. → Nico said…
items.a: Nico said (that) it was the best pizza he had ever had.

items.q: He told that he had finished.
items.a: He said (that) he had finished. / He told me (that) he had finished.

items.q: Last month Ana said she will call me, but she never did.
items.a: Last month Ana said she would call me, but she never did.

items.q: He said he would came early.
items.a: He said he would come early.

items.q: He said: “that he was hungry.”
My sister told to me that she was pregnant.
items.a: My sister told me (that) she was pregnant.

items.q: They said that they had arrived two days ago.
items.a: They said that they had arrived two days before (earlier).

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el artículo. Marca T (true) o F (false) y contesta las preguntas.
exercises.en: Read the article. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: Last week our reporter met Daniel Ruiz, the 24-year-old chef who has just opened his first restaurant in Brighton. Daniel told us that he had always wanted to be a chef. He said he had learnt to cook with his grandmother in Málaga when he was eight.
He said that the first months had been really hard: he was working fourteen hours a day and he hadn't had a day off since March. However, he said he loved every minute of it.

As for the future, he said he was going to open a second restaurant in London the following year. He also said he would never forget his grandmother's advice: “Cook with love, and people will come back.”

items.q: Daniel's restaurant is in London.
items.why: It's in Brighton; the London one will be his second restaurant.

items.q: He learnt to cook when he was a child.
He has had several days off since March.
items.why: He said he hadn't had a day off since March.

items.q: He doesn't enjoy his work.
items.why: He said he loved every minute of it.

items.q: What did Daniel say about his grandmother?
items.a: He said he had learnt to cook with her in Málaga when he was eight.

items.q: Write Daniel's plans in direct speech: “I…”
items.a: “I'm going to open a second restaurant in London next year.”

items.q: Find in the text the reported form of next year.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Cuenta lo que te dijeron otras personas. Usa said y told y da el paso atrás.
exercises.en: Report what other people told you.

items.q: Algo que te dijo un amigo la semana pasada: My friend … told me…
items.a: Ej.: My friend Leo told me he was going to move to Valencia. He said he had found a job there.

items.q: Dos cosas que te dijo un profesor o tu jefe/a hace tiempo.
items.a: Ej.: My English teacher said we had to read every day. She told us practice was the key.

items.q: Una noticia que hayas leído: The minister said that…
items.a: Ej.: The minister said that the new train line would open the following year.

items.q: Un mensaje a un amigo contando lo que dijo otra persona (cambia tiempo, pronombre y expresión de tiempo).
items.a: Ej.: Hi Sam! Ana called last week. She said she had lost her phone and that she would buy a new one the next day.
